label: Family
tagline: For Christmas, holidays and Sunday afternoons.
name: The Family Game

chance.text: It is Sunday. Go to Start for your pocket money. Collect 200 from the bank.
Grandma calls you over to {24}. Go there. If you pass Start on the way, take 200 from the bank.
There are pancakes at {11}. Go there. If you pass Start on the way, take 200 from the bank.
The fuse trips. Go to {12} or {28}, whichever is closer. If someone owns it, pay 10 times your last throw.
The family car is full. Go to the nearest transport space. If someone owns it, pay double rent.
The bus to Grandma's just drove off. Go to the nearest transport space. If someone owns it, pay double rent.
You win at cards against Grandpa.
Mum sorts it out for you. Keep this card. You can use it once to get out of jail.
You cycle the wrong way. Go back three spaces.
You took sweets from the jar. Go to jail right away, without passing Start.
Grandma's house needs doing up. Pay 30 per house and 120 per hotel.
You break a cup from the good china. That costs you money.
Everyone is already in {5}. Go there. If you pass Start on the way, take 200 from the bank.
You invite everyone for dinner. Pay each player 40.
Auntie slips a note into your hand.
The family is waiting at {39}. Go there.

chest.text: The party starts at Start. Collect your pocket money. Collect 200 from the bank.
Grandpa won the lottery and shares it out.
You drop the cake on the floor.
You get your money back for the bike you lent out.
Grandma knows someone. Keep this card. You can use it once to get out of jail.
You ate the last biscuit and lied about it. Go to jail right away, without passing Start.
You win the card game on Christmas Eve.
You find a twenty in an old jacket.
You tell a lovely family story. Each player chips in 10.
You get your share of the inheritance.
You pay for the family dinner for everyone.
You get a refund for the caravan.
After the family party everything needs tidying. Pay 35 per house and 100 per hotel.
You find loose change in the couch.

houseRules: The youngest player may pick one rule per round.
Arguing over a street? The oldest person at the table decides.
Whoever buys a street shares a memory of that place.
